newsitem.title: USA: Sepracor approved for S-oxybutynin study.
newsitem.headline: Sepracor approved for S-oxybutynin study.

text.p: Sepracor Inc said it received U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance to start a Phase I study of S-oxybutynin to treat urinary incontinence.
The study will start immediately, a company spokeswoman said.

The study's aim is to show S-oxybutynin, marketed as Ditropan by Hoechst AG's Hoechst Marion Roussel and also sold generically, does not prompt dry mouth, nausea and cardiac palpitation side effects, the company said.
Pending the study's outcome, the company may market the drug itself or form a partnership to do so, the spokeswoman said.
